console.name: Manzel Console
console.tagline: Everything that runs Manzel, in one place.

shell.signOutBody: Alerts stop on this browser. To come back you will need a new code from your email and one from your authenticator app.
shell.offline: You are offline. What you see may be out of date.
shell.installBody: Open it from your home screen or dock like an app, and receive alerts.
shell.installIos: On iPhone or iPad: tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.
shell.updateReady: A new version of the console is ready.

auth.title: Sign in to the console
auth.body: For the people who run Manzel. Use the email on your Manzel account.
auth.sentBody: If {{email}} belongs to an operator, a 6-digit code is on its way.
auth.checkSpam: Not there after a minute? Check your spam folder.
auth.codeInvalid: That code is wrong or has expired. Check it, or send a new one.
auth.invalidEmail: That does not look like an email address.
auth.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.
auth.notOperator: This account is not an operator
auth.notOperatorBody: The console is only for the people who run Manzel. You are signed in as {{email}}.
auth.phoneOnly: No email on your account? Add one in the Manzel app under Settings → Sign-in email, then come back.
auth.secure: Sign-in needs your email and an authenticator app. Nothing here works without both.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.challengeBody: Open your authenticator app and type the 6-digit code for Manzel.
mfa.codeInvalid: That code is not right. Codes change every 30 seconds — try the newest one.
mfa.setupBody: Operators can change anything in Manzel, so the console asks for a code from an authenticator app every time you sign in — a stolen email alone opens nothing.
mfa.step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone: Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or any app that shows 6-digit codes.
mfa.step2: In the app, add an account and scan this code.
mfa.step3: Type the 6-digit code the app now shows.
mfa.cantScan: Cannot scan? Type this key into the app instead:
mfa.lostDevice: Lost the phone with your authenticator? Another operator can reset it for you from your page in People.
mfa.addAnotherBody: A second phone, as a spare: if one is lost, the other still signs you in.
mfa.removeBody: Its codes will stop working for your account.
mfa.lastFactor: This is your only authenticator. Add a spare before removing it.
mfa.statusOff: Not set up yet: it is set up at the first sign-in to the console.
mfa.resetBody: Their authenticators stop working. At their next sign-in to the console they set up a new one. Do this only when you are sure it is them asking.
mfa.resetHint: For an operator who lost the phone with their authenticator.

account.title: My account
account.subtitle: How you sign in, and how the console looks for you.
account.signOutEverywhereBody: The console, and the Manzel app on every phone where this account is signed in, will ask to sign in again. Alerts stop on every browser.
account.openInApp: Your name and phone are changed in the Manzel app.

list.noResultsBody: Try other words or fewer filters.
list.name: Name
list.notFound: Not found. It may have been removed.

errors.pageBody: The page could not be shown. Try again; if it keeps happening, the activity log may say why.
errors.notFoundBody: This address does not lead anywhere in the console.

buildings.openedInApp: You can now manage {{name}} in the Manzel app: open the app on your phone and choose the building.

support.chooseBody: Waiting conversations are first. Answering one makes it yours.
support.enterHint: Enter sends · Shift+Enter for a new line
support.tooBig: That file is too big (10 MB at most).

apps.subtitle: Which version of the app is on which phone, and who is up to date.
apps.emptyBody: A phone appears here once someone opens the app on it.
apps.howCounted: An app from before this version says only its version — not its build, phone or update — so its phone shows with less detail.

target.title: Which apps
target.noVersions: No app has said its version yet.
target.hint: Each app says its version as it opens.
target.belowHint: An app that never said its version counts as older.
target.atLeastHint: An app that never said its version is left out.
target.bannerHint: A banner for some apps only: an update notice for the old ones, say. Every app checks with the server, the old ones too.

alerts.subtitle: How the platform tells you that something needs you: by email, and on this browser.
alerts.unsupportedBody: On an iPhone or iPad, install the console first: Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.
alerts.unconfigured: Alerts are not set up yet
alerts.unconfiguredBody: The console needs its push key (NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY). See the deployment guide.
alerts.blocked: Alerts are blocked in this browser
alerts.blockedBody: Allow notifications for this site in the browser's settings, then come back.
alerts.offBody: Turn them on and this browser shows each alert, even with the console closed.
alerts.onBody: Each alert shows on this browser, in this language, until you turn them off or sign out.
alerts.turnedOn: Alerts are on in this browser.
alerts.turnedOff: Alerts are off in this browser.
alerts.testSent: Test sent: an email to admin@ and a push to your consoles.
alerts.rateLimited: Five tests in ten minutes is enough. Try again later.
alerts.emailTitle: Every alert goes by email too
alerts.emailUnset: Email is not set up yet
alerts.emailUnsetBody: The operator-alerts function needs the mailbox's SMTP details (ALERTS_SMTP_*). See the deployment guide.
alerts.pushUnset: Push is not set up on the server yet
alerts.pushUnsetBody: The operator-alerts function needs the VAPID keys (VAPID_*). See the deployment guide.
alerts.emptyBody: A support message, a building request, an idea or a report shows up here the moment it arrives.
alerts.homeOff: Alerts are off on this browser
alerts.homeOffBody: Turn them on to hear of a support message, a building request or a report the moment it arrives, even with the console closed.

push.againTitle: A copy of a notification already sent
push.againBody: Everything is filled in as it was sent, for the same people. Change what you need, check who gets it, and send.
